title: ForceZero of init_op after every cipher/HMAC: key material cleaned from stack
description:
Both crypto2dev_cipher() and crypto2dev_hmac() call ForceZero(&init_op, sizeof(init_op)) at the done: label, which runs on both success and error paths. The init_op struct contains the raw AES or HMAC key in plaintext.

A future contributor might remove this as 'unnecessary cleanup since the function returns anyway' or replace it with XMEMSET. Neither is correct: ForceZero is defined to be non-optimizable-away (it uses volatile writes), while XMEMSET may be elided by the compiler on dead-store elimination. The stack zeroization is a deliberate security property.

Why this choice is correct: The key lives on the stack in init_op.key for the duration of the ioctl call. Without ForceZero, the key bytes remain in stack memory until overwritten by the next function call, and can be read from core dumps, /proc/self/mem, or speculation-based side channels. ForceZero prevents this. This is the correct function to use, not XMEMSET.
